title: Alabama AI Laws

reading.body:
Alabama has passed two AI-related laws, and neither one regulates AI as a general technology: one governs AI in health insurance denials, the other creates a study commission on children and the internet.

The pattern is narrow and sectoral. SB63 is the only binding obligation in the set. It applies to health benefit plan providers making medical necessity determinations for prior authorization, and it requires individualized clinical review, annual certification, human clinician final decisions on denials, disclosure, periodic review, and data protections, with the Department of Insurance able to investigate and discipline violations. HJR51 imposes nothing on anyone. It creates a commission to study AI, social media, and internet access as they affect children, to examine other states' approaches, and to report to the Legislature by November 1, 2026, after which it dissolves.

For AI specifically, the split matters more than the count. A two-law total suggests activity, but only one law changes what an operator must do, and only inside a single regulated industry. The other is a recommendation pipeline, and its output is a report, not a rule. Anyone reading the count as a measure of Alabama's AI oversight would be overstating it.

What this data does not cover is the rest of the picture. It says nothing about federal law, local ordinances, or bills that failed, and nothing about how the two laws are enforced in practice. It also carries no information about data centers, electricity, or computing capacity in Alabama, so it cannot speak to whether the state's grid or its buildings constrain AI development there. The commission's November 2026 report is the next dated event in this set, and its contents are not yet known.

Alabama has enacted 2 AI-related laws. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Alabama

2 laws this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • SB63: Health care plans; to regulate the use of artificial intelligence in determinations of coverage passed 2026-04-17

    This Alabama law limits how health benefit plan providers may use artificial intelligence to make medical necessity determinations for prior authorization requests. It requires individualized clinical review, annual certification, human clinician final decisions on denials, disclosure, periodic review, and data protections. The Department of Insurance may investigate and discipline violations.

  • HJR51: Artificial Intelligence and Children's Internet Safety Study Commission, created passed 2026-03-10

    Creates the Study Commission on Artificial Intelligence and Children's Internet Safety to study the effects of artificial intelligence, social media, and Internet access on children, investigate other states' approaches, and develop recommendations for potential legislation. The commission must report to the Legislature by November 1, 2026, and then dissolves.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Alabama. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
